theme.title: Mixed / Stock-Picker's Market
theme.summary: Health Care (+0.45%) and Consumer Staples (+0.23%) led the market today, while Communication Svcs (-1.52%) and Consumer Discretionary (-1.26%) brought up the rear. That split lines up with a rotation out of growth: growth-oriented sectors averaged -1.25% versus -0.06% for defensives and -0.56% for value and cyclicals, suggesting money moved from high-multiple names into steadier, cash-generative businesses. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 -0.63%, Dow -0.60%, Nasdaq -0.74% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps moved roughly in line with the broader market, with the Russell 2000 at -0.42%. The VIX rose 6.86% to 15.89, pointing to a bit more caution creeping in beneath the surface. Gold slipped 1.36% to $4,172.80, crude oil was little changed at $92.52, and bitcoin slipped 0.88% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
